6. Outlier-Adjusted Probabilistic Safety Verification Approach
The verification methods in Sections 4 and 5 are limited by the quality of the neural reachable tube.
Although they can account for outliers, the computed safety level can be low if the outlier rate is
high. This can lead to significant losses in the safe volume, as demonstrated in Sections 6.2 and 6.3.
To address this issue, we propose an outlier-adjusted approach that can recover a larger safe
volume for any desired ϵ. Note that in the verification methods, the key quantity which determines ϵ
is the number of safety violations k. This corresponds to the number of samples xi which are marked
safe by membership in S, i.e., ˜V (xi, 0) ≥δ, but are not guaranteed to be safe, i.e., J˜π (xi, 0) ≤0.
It is easy to see that the best we can do to simultaneously minimize k and maximize volume is to
compute S as the super-δ level set of the induced cost function J˜π(x, 0). For example, the largest
possible S that is guaranteed to be violation-free is precisely the super-zero level set of J˜π(x, 0).
Thus, our overall approach will be to refine ˜V (x, 0) so that it more accurately reflects J˜π(x, 0).

Although they can account for outliers, the computed safety level can be low if the outlier rate is high. This can lead to significant losses in the safe volume, as demonstrated in Sections 6.2 and 6.3.
